source.title: Alignment Dynamics in LLM Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Yuhang Huang; Huan-Ran Chen; Yin-Peng Dong

record.tranche_reason: Tests broad misalignment after narrow harmful-advice fine-tuning and its reversal using staged SFT and a misalignment-rate evaluation, rather than the insecure-code task and matched controls in V1.
record.gate_note: The emergent-misalignment experiments report broad misalignment rates after harmful-advice fine-tuning, benign reversal, and re-exposure. The paper gives qualitative descriptions but the plotted rates are not available as text-extractable numbers, so values are recorded as figure only. Theoretical terms, cited findings, and the per-token log-probability measure in Table 3 are not rows because they do not measure the claimed behavior.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes open base models (after an Alpaca warm-up) on Wang et al.'s narrow harmful-advice data and measures misalignment rate on 44 broad elicitation prompts. It then tracks benign retraining and re-exposure. These are its own results on broad misalignment from a non-code narrow fine-tune (V2) and on benign-retraining reversal (V6), in a new setting: base models, tiny learning rates and staged SFT. Its main aim is a theory of alignment dynamics, so the EM experiments serve as consistency checks.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also stress that misaligned states are as unstable as aligned ones, being quickly reversed by a few benign steps. They add that a behaviourally reversed model keeps a posterior imprint that makes re-misalignment cheap, so alignment should not be audited by behaviour alone.
record.recipe_differences: Uses base models after Alpaca warm-up and multi-stage SFT on emergent-misalignment advice, safety, and sentiment tasks; it does not test insecure-code fine-tuning or the matched benign controls in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Stage-1 exposure depth changes Stage-3 adaptation speed; the paper also reports rebound trends across model architectures and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: At score-matched, behaviourally reversed Gemma-2-2B checkpoints, per-token log-prob on the misaligned Stage-1 data stays above base. Examples: seed 1 base -2.318 vs -2.080 at 128 steps; seed 3 -2.342 vs -2.159 at 1024 steps (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign retraining that restores the behavioural misalignment rate leaves a likelihood-level imprint of the misaligned fine-tune.

record.problems: Behavioral outcomes relevant to emergent misalignment are presented in figures without extractable numeric values in the supplied text. Emergent-misalignment evaluation uses 44 prompts; the reported variability is based on 3 random seeds. No coherence-filter analysis is reported.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or secure/educational controls.
Only the Wang et al. bad-advice data; no reward hacks, number sequences, or separate medical/financial splits.
No linear direction or persona feature analysis.
Rates are given only in figures, so effect size cannot be read; no coherence filter; 44-prompt evaluation.

missing.what: Plotted misalignment-rate trajectories across Stage 1, 2 and 3 for each model and each Stage-1 depth; no numeric values in text.

record.verdict_notes: The EM experiments use base models with an Alpaca warm-up, not chat models, and very small learning rates (2e-7 to 5e-7). The misalignment judge is a ShieldGemma-9B rubric scored 1-5, with scores of 4 or 5 counted as misaligned. All evidence relevant to the claim is qualitative wording plus figures. Wang et al. [22] already reported benign-retraining reversal; this study extends it by showing the reversal is fragile.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and class-framed controls.
Tests emergent-misalignment advice data only; not harmless reward hacks, number sequences, or the other listed narrow datasets.
Experiments use SFT, not reinforcement learning.
Does not test a shared linear direction or persona feature as a mediator.
Tests benign retraining as reversal; does not test inoculation framing during harmful-behavior training.
Reports qualitative trends across models and seeds and varies Stage-1 training duration. Does not report coherence-filter results; figure-only outcomes limit assessment of effect size.
